jobs.title: Business Operations Associate
jobs.description:
BUSINESS OPERATIONS ASSOCIATE



Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.




THE ROLE



Rebuilding a business as software only works if the business actually runs while you rebuild it. Underwriters need answers. Carriers need data. Sales needs enablement. Customers need follow-ups. Today a lot of that runs on people keeping track of things in their heads — and that breaks at ~1,000 new customers a month.



Your job is to learn the entire operation — not one slice — and turn what's in people's heads into systems that scale. One day you're chasing a stalled quote with an underwriter. The next you're building the process that makes sure no quote stalls again. The day after, you're on a customer call, then feeding what you heard into a product spec. The patterns you spot become the things engineering builds next.



No two weeks look the same, and that's the point. You'll rotate across sales enablement, underwriting operations, customer service, and carrier relations — owning real work in each, not observing. The scope is wide because the company moves fast and the problems don't respect org charts.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Run the operation. Underwriter follow-ups, carrier communications, keeping deals moving through the pipeline.

 - Build systems that scale. Create the processes, workflows, and structures that make the team faster — and make manual work obsolete.

 - Own relationships on both sides. Be the person who makes sure nothing falls through the cracks with customers or underwriters.

 - Enable sales. Arm the team with the data, materials, and feedback loops they need to close.

 - Touch the full lifecycle. Intake, onboarding, servicing, renewals — you'll see how the whole business works.

 - Shape what gets built. Translate operational pain into product requirements with engineering.

 - Move where it's urgent. Context-switch across functions based on what matters most this week.




WHO YOU ARE



 - You've been the best at something — top of your class, captain of the team, first in your cohort — and you're looking for the next thing to pour that into.

 - At every past job you ended up doing more than your title said.

 - You get energy from moving fast across many problems, not sitting in one lane.

 - You'd rather own a messy problem end-to-end than execute a clean task someone handed you.

 - You context-switch without losing intensity, and you care about outcomes over job descriptions.



Requirements: 1–3 years in a high-pace environment (startup, consulting, banking, operations, or equivalent); strong written and verbal communication with customers, underwriters, and internal teams; comfort pulling insight from a spreadsheet and making a call; bias toward action; based in SF or willing to relocate immediately.



Nice to have: prior startup or founder experience; insurance, fintech, or regulated-industry exposure; familiarity with CRM, workflow automation, or AI-assisted tooling; background in sales, customer success, or account management.




THE HONEST DAY-TO-DAY



 - It's execution, not strategy-from-a-desk. A real share of the week is follow-ups, chasing, coordination, and cleanup — the operational backbone, done well. The system-building is earned by doing the unglamorous work first.

 - Ambiguity is the job, not a phase. Scope shifts week to week. If you need a fixed lane and a clean spec, you'll be uncomfortable here.

 - Long days, on-site. Mon–Fri, roughly 5 AM–8 PM, in person in SF.

 - The ceiling is high and real. People who are exceptional here go on to run functions, lead teams, or start companies — because they've seen how the whole business works. That's the payoff, and it's on the other side of the grind.




COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS



 - Salary: $110,000–$140,000 + performance bonuses & equity

 - Location: San Francisco, in-office. Based in SF or willing to relocate immediately.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, in-office hours matching the rest of the company.

 - Benefits: Uber commuter benefits; breakfast, lunch, and dinner provided; snacks, drinks, and coffee daily; free gym membership; health, dental, and vision insurance.




PROCESS



 1. People screen — initial fit and alignment

 2. Lead screen — skills and culture fit

 3. Super day — case exercise and hands-on work with the team




TO APPLY



Send your resume and tell us about a time you owned something messy and made it work. If you've been waiting for the opportunity that finally matches your ability, this is it.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Lead
jobs.description:
REVENUE OPERATIONS LEAD



Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.






THE ROLE



Two dashboards disagree about the same funnel. A stage changed without the owner changing. The forecast moved and nobody can trace why. Those are not reporting annoyances. They are failures in the operating system you own.



Here is the honest state of it: Harper has been piecing RevOps together as it grew — a routing rule here, a dashboard there, a forecast someone built because the company needed one that week. It got us to ~100x growth. It will not get us through the next stage. We need someone who has actually run revenue operations before, who knows what a canonical funnel definition looks like and why a CRM automation needs a failure state, and who will take permanent ownership of the definitions, system behavior, routing, forecast, and instrumentation underneath Harper's revenue. When another team proves a temporary fix, you decide how it enters the permanent system, and you keep it reconciled.



Why now: Harper is scaling across three offices. Atlanta adds frontline volume, New York adds a second headquarters, and this San Francisco seat keeps one inspectable revenue system underneath all of it. This role does not own frontline sales management, customer conversations, placement strategy, or marketing creative. It owns the system those teams run on.






WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Own the funnel definitions. Maintain the canonical meaning, entry rule, exit rule, source, and accountable owner for every revenue state, so there is one answer to what a stage means.

 - Own CRM behavior and routing. Define and maintain fields, validations, automations, permissions, and state transitions, and keep assignment logic, exceptions, ownership changes, and escalation paths inspectable and tested. Every routing change carries a test case, an approval owner, an effective date, and a rollback path.

 - Own the forecast. Publish the method, inputs, assumptions, and version, and carry the variance back to actual booked revenue every cycle.

 - Own revenue instrumentation. Make demand, contact, intake, quote, close, bind, and booked revenue reconcile to their source records for the same population and window.

 - Run funnel analysis and turn it into action. Find where volume, conversion, speed, or handoffs break, and convert the finding into a specific operating change with a named owner.

 - Automate repeat work with controls. Use enrichment, generated notes, task creation, quality checks, and reporting only when the source, resulting state, failure state, and human correction path stay visible.

 - Measure the change. Prove whether a workflow, campaign, routing decision, or sales motion moved conversion, speed, or revenue — and say so plainly when it didn't.






WHO YOU ARE



 - You have owned revenue operations, sales operations, or growth operations at a fast-growing company. This is the real background we've been missing, not a nice-to-have.

 - You understand CRM architecture, lifecycle stages, routing, attribution, forecasting, and pipeline hygiene from the inside.

 - You can write SQL, or work directly enough with the data to test a claim yourself before you repeat it.

 - You move from analysis to operating change and then measure whether the change worked.

 - You can partner with sales leaders and frontline operators — working inside the sales, intake, placement, and service workflows before changing them — without turning every problem into a process meeting.

 - You treat AI as leverage — you've operated generated notes, enrichment, routing, or reporting automations with visible source data, failure states, and correction paths — and you have opinions about where it helps and where it quietly corrupts the record.

 - You care more about booked revenue and conversion than dashboard activity.






THE REALITY — READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY



This job is on-site in San Francisco, Monday through Friday, long days, in the building with sales, intake, and placement, with travel to Atlanta and New York as the offices scale. You are inheriting a system that was assembled under pressure by people whose real jobs were something else. The first months are archaeology: finding every definition that drifted, every automation nobody owns, every report that doesn't reconcile, and fixing them while revenue keeps moving through the pipe. There is no pause button and no clean handoff.



If you want to administer a CRM without owning the revenue outcome, if you produce reports but don't make operating recommendations, if you want to own sales management, account placement, or marketing creative, or if you treat field completeness as proof that the underlying process works, this seat will frustrate you. It does not come with a remote or hybrid default. If the intensity reads as a cost you'd rather avoid, this isn't the seat. If it reads as the point, keep going.






COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS



 - Salary: 170,000–240,000 base, plus performance bonus and equity.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco. Based there or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, long days. Exact coverage window is set by office.






BENEFITS



 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Meals provided — breakfast, lunch, and dinner

 - Snacks, drinks, and coffee stocked daily

 - Commuter benefits

 - Free gym membership






PROCESS



 1. Team call — 30 minutes on Zoom. You meet the team, we meet you.

 2. Office session — about two hours in person. You meet more of the team and work a real problem with us.

 3. Super day — how you actually operate, in real time. We decide after this.

The process moves as fast as you do.






TO APPLY



Send your resume and one revenue-operations example: a funnel or CRM problem that looked like a data issue but was really an operating issue, how you proved it, what you changed, and the revenue or conversion result.

jobs.title: Head of Partnerships
jobs.description:
HEAD OF PARTNERSHIPS



Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.




THE ROLE



Harper turns small-business owners into covered customers at volume, with AI doing the heavy lifting behind the human who closes. We've grown ~100x in a year. The constraint isn't demand. It's getting in front of the right business at the moment buying insurance stops being optional. That's where this role lives.



You'll build distribution at forcing mechanisms: the regulators, lenders, landlords, franchisors, and trusted advisors who make coverage non-optional for a business. Whoever owns that moment owns the highest-intent customer in the market, and your job is to plug Harper into them and turn each one into a channel that compounds. This is the playbook behind the best distribution businesses (payments networks, commerce platforms, marketplaces): find the installed base, mandate, or transaction moment that carries a product to the customer exactly when they need it. You don't need an insurance background to see the shape of it. You need to have built distribution somewhere.



It's a founding-leader seat reporting to the CEO, in growth and biz-ops, not marketing or pure sales. You start hands-on and earn a team by proving the motion.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Close the first marquee partners yourself, structure the economics, and write the playbook from live deals.

 - Decide which channels to build and in what order, and say no to the rest.

 - Build the attribution, payouts, and contracts so every partner-sourced dollar is tracked.

 - Route every referral to a named owner with a tracked outcome.

 - Design partner economics counsel can clear before launch, and keep the regulated path fast.

 - Own the scoreboard: partner-sourced conversion, revenue per partner, time-to-first-referral, reviewed weekly with the CEO.

 - Hire an execution lead and build the team once the motion is proven.




WHO YOU ARE



 - You think in distribution, not logos.

 - You're a player-coach: you'll close deals this quarter and build the team next year.

 - You're rigorous about attribution and unit economics, including thin-margin, high-volume models.

 - You move cross-functional work across product, legal, compliance, and ops without owning those teams.

 - You treat regulation as a design problem, not a blocker.

 - You learn a new domain fast and use AI as real leverage.




REQUIREMENTS



 - A track record building distribution, channel, or platform partnerships that drove attributable revenue, at a payments, commerce, fintech, marketplace, or platform company (or somewhere equally complex).

 - You've personally closed and structured partner deals, not just managed a team that did.

 - Comfort with low-margin, high-volume unit economics.

 - Based in SF or willing to relocate; on-site, with travel to partner markets.




NICE TO HAVE



 - Insurance, insurtech, or other regulated-distribution experience (useful, never required).

 - Embedded or API distribution, developer/ISV ecosystems, or marketplace app stores.

 - Channel or reseller program design.

 - A regulated launch navigated with counsel.




THE REALITY



This is a build-from-zero seat, not a big-company partnerships seat. No team, no pipeline, no brand opening doors. You are the brand, and the first quarter is you closing deals yourself. The deals are small and the discipline is high, so small-dollar, high-volume economics have to energize you. It's on-site in San Francisco, long days, Monday to Friday, with travel when the work calls for it. Almost no one takes this job for insurance. They take it because owning distribution from zero at a company growing ~100x is about as close to founding something as you can get without leaving.




COMPENSATION



 - Salary: $190,000 to $260,000 base, plus a milestone-based variable tied to partner-sourced revenue, plus meaningful equity.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco. Based here or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday to Friday, long days, on-site, with travel to partner markets as needed.




BENEFITS



 - Uber commuter benefits

 - Meals provided: breakfast, lunch, and dinner

 - Snacks, drinks, and coffee stocked daily

 - Free gym membership

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance




THE PROCESS



 1. Lead screen - Fit and alignment.

 2. Founder screen with the CEO - How you think about distribution at a forcing mechanism.

 3. Super day - Work a live partner pitch and present a partnership you built.




TO APPLY



Send your resume and one partnership or distribution channel you built yourself: who the partner was, the forcing mechanism it sat on, the economics you structured, and how you know it worked.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
THE PROBLEM



36 million businesses in America need insurance—it's not optional. 77% are underinsured. 40% have no coverage at all. The distribution system failed them: too slow, too opaque, too confusing.



Over 90% of commercial insurance is still human-led. We're building the inverse: 90%+ AI-led, pushing toward the higher 90s. Not by patching legacy workflows—by building AI that makes humans more effective, improves the customer experience, and eliminates friction at every step.

We're adding ~1,000 customers per month. We've grown 100x since last year. We're looking to do even more this year—and that's why we're hiring.



You own the engine that turns those 36 million problems into a full pipeline—from the first click to a bound policy.




THE THESIS



Growth is Harper's engine for turning demand into coverage. Leads come in through a dozen different surfaces—web, aggregators, social, paid, and everything in between—and every one of them needs to make it through intake to a completed policy. That means two problems that have to work in lockstep: consistently filling the top of the funnel, and having the capacity to carry every lead through to completion.



We're pushing to make this as AI-forward as the rest of Harper. The team has spent the last stretch architecting Voice AI systems that can run intake at the volume our funnel demands—this is where most of the technical complexity in the role lives, and where the leverage compounds. Get intake capacity right, and every channel you turn on downstream just works.




THE ROLE



You'll own Growth end to end: the acquisition side—web, aggregators, social, paid, and every other distribution surface, organic and non-organic—built in close partnership with our growth and marketing teams, and the intake side, where leads move through the requirements needed to get bound. The north star is simple: a consistent, reliable supply of leads across every channel, and the capacity to run every one of them through intake to completion.



The team is 5 people today and we're aiming to roughly 2x it to around 10 over the next three months. Managing individuals and actively shaping their careers is core to this job, not a side responsibility—and you'll work in close partnership with growth marketing, sales, and operations, so stakeholder management matters as much as team management.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Own the Growth org — lead and grow a team from 5 to ~10 over the next three months, with day-to-day management and career development as a core part of the job

 - Drive lead acquisition — partner closely with growth and marketing on every distribution surface: web, aggregators, social, paid, and beyond, organic and non-organic

 - Own intake capacity — make sure every lead that enters the funnel can be taken through intake and completed to bound coverage

 - Architect Voice AI for scale — this is where most of the team's technical complexity sits; build the systems that let intake keep up with demand

 - Partner across the business — work in lockstep with growth marketing, sales, and operations as a primary stakeholder group

 - Stay hands-on — keep the team unblocked, help shape architecture, dive into code when they're stuck, and write code yourself when it's needed

 - Hire the team — build out from 5 to 10, drawing on your own network where you can




YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF...



 - You've been a line manager for at least two years, directly managing teams of 6+ people

 - You come from a product-first company, in a product-first role

 - You've optimized growth funnels end to end, from top of funnel to bottom

 - You've worked in an operations-heavy environment and are comfortable partnering with non-technical stakeholders

 - You're not afraid to get your hands dirty—diving into code when the team needs it, not just directing from above

 - You move fast, and expect your team to as well




NICE TO HAVE



 - A track record of hiring and building out a team from scratch, with your own network to draw from

 - Experience with Voice AI or other real-time/conversational AI systems

 - Experience partnering directly with growth marketing and sales in a high-velocity, operations-heavy business

 - Prior startup experience—especially at a company scaling through hyper growth




COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS



 - Salary: $225,000–$275,000

 - Location: San Francisco, in-office. Based in SF or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, in-office five days a week.

 - Benefits: Uber commuter benefits; breakfast, lunch, and dinner provided; snacks, drinks, and coffee daily; free gym membership; health, dental, and vision insurance.




THE PROCESS



 1. Hiring Manager screen - 30 min video chat.

 2. Technical screen — 60 min remote: project deep dive + system design

 3. Super Day on-site — meet the team, sit in on the operation, do real work alongside us.

jobs.title: Carrier Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
CARRIER PARTNERSHIPS LEAD



Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.






THE ROLE



One appointment can open an industry. One weak escalation path can leave hundreds of accounts stuck behind the same underwriting desk. Harper's AI is generating more qualified demand than most brokerages see in a decade, and demand only matters if there are carriers, wholesalers, MGAs, and programs willing and able to take it. You own those relationships at the portfolio level: access, appointments, capacity, economics, senior relationships, and the escalation channels that get a stuck account moving.



This is a relationship job, done on foot. You are the face of Harper to each carrier, and you stomp the ground with them day in and day out. You send carriers their urgency list — what we need quoted this week, what's stuck, what's about to be lost. You track outstanding binds and upcoming renewals across every market and make sure the carrier sees them before they become a problem. You know who controls appetite, capacity, and operations at each partner, and they know you. What you do not do is place accounts: the licensed account team selects the market, negotiates terms, and makes the recommendation on each one. You build the doors they walk through and the phone number they call when a door sticks.



Why now: Harper is expanding its insurance reach across offices and lines, and the constraint is shifting from demand to market access. Carrier trust, appointments, and capacity get more important as the machine gets better at producing submissions, not less.






WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Build and keep the market map. Know Harper's carriers, wholesalers, MGAs, programs, appointments, constraints, and real production path by line, class, and state — and keep relationship history, agreements, appetite changes, contacts, and commitments current.

 - Open the right doors. Win appointments, preferred access, new programs, and senior relationships where Harper has credible demand, and take each effort to a real decision instead of leaving it open.

 - Be the face of Harper to each carrier. Own the relationship with the people who control appetite, capacity, operations, and distribution strategy. Show up, in person and on the phone, until they think of Harper first.

 - Run the urgency list. Send each carrier what needs attention now — pending quotes, outstanding binds, upcoming renewals, stuck submissions — and track it until it's cleared.

 - Turn demand into a carrier case. Show carriers the volume, risk mix, submission quality, conversion, and operating capability that justify deeper access, then negotiate the commissions, fees, service expectations, data exchange, and escalation paths Harper can support.

 - Manage portfolio performance. Track what Harper sends, what markets quote, what binds, where service breaks, and which relationships deserve more investment. Carrier reviews tie relationship effort to sent, quoted, bound, response, and service outcomes.

 - Create clean escalation paths. Make sure account-level teams know exactly who to call and how to move a stuck issue, without taking over their ownership of the account.






WHO YOU ARE



 - You've built carrier, wholesaler, MGA, or distribution partnerships in commercial insurance, and you've personally opened and developed senior insurance relationships.

 - You know how appointments, programs, commissions, capacity, and distribution economics actually work.

 - You understand the difference between a signed agreement and a relationship that produces, and you measure yourself on the second.

 - You can turn operating data into a credible carrier-development case and negotiate from it.

 - You're commercially aggressive without making promises the operation can't keep.

 - You treat AI as leverage — it builds the urgency list, pulls the production data, and preps the carrier review — and you spend the time it saves in front of the carrier.

 - You can work closely with account teams, underwriters, and market partners while keeping portfolio relationship ownership clearly yours.






THE REALITY — READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY



This job is on-site in San Francisco, Monday through Friday, long days, with travel to carriers, wholesalers, and industry events when the relationship calls for it. Much of the week is unglamorous: chasing an outstanding bind, re-sending an urgency list, tracking a renewal nobody else is watching, and doing it again tomorrow with a different carrier. Relationships here are built on showing up consistently and producing, not on dinners. You will have a production scoreboard, and it will be visible.



If you want to be a relationship manager without a scoreboard, if you measure success by meetings, logos, or signed agreements that don't change placement outcomes, if you want to own individual account negotiation instead of the carrier portfolio, or if you expect the underwriting or brokerage teams to maintain your relationship records for you, this seat will frustrate you. This is not a consumer acquisition or demand-generation role, and it does not come with a remote or hybrid default. If the intensity reads as a cost you'd rather avoid, this isn't the seat. If it reads as the point, keep going.






COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS



 - Salary: 150,000–220,000 base, plus variable tied to carrier outcomes, plus equity.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco. Based there or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, long days. Exact coverage window is set by office.






BENEFITS



 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Meals provided — breakfast, lunch, and dinner

 - Snacks, drinks, and coffee stocked daily

 - Commuter benefits

 - Free gym membership






PROCESS



 1. Team call — 30 minutes on Zoom. You meet the team, we meet you.

 2. Office session — about two hours in person. You meet more of the team and work a real problem with us.

 3. Super day — how you actually operate, in real time. We decide after this.

The process moves as fast as you do.






TO APPLY



Send your resume and one carrier-partnership case: a carrier, wholesaler, or program relationship you personally opened or changed, the commercial reason it mattered, what you negotiated, and the production result.

jobs.title: HR Generalist
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities

1. Talent Acquisition & Recruiting

 - Manage the end-to-end recruitment process, from role intake and sourcing to offer management and closing candidates.

 - Partner with hiring managers to understand hiring needs, define role requirements, and develop effective recruiting strategies.

 - Source and engage candidates through LinkedIn, referrals, job boards, and other relevant channels.

 - Screen candidates, coordinate interviews, gather feedback, and ensure a smooth and timely hiring process.

 - Build and maintain strong candidate pipelines for current and future hiring needs.

 - Deliver a positive candidate experience through clear communication and timely follow-ups.

 - Manage offer rollouts, coordinate pre-employment documentation, and partner with hiring managers to close candidates.

 - Track recruiting metrics, hiring progress, and pipeline health.

 - Continuously improve recruiting processes, sourcing strategies, and employer branding initiatives.

2. HR Operations & Employee Lifecycle

 - Manage employee lifecycle processes, including onboarding, employee changes, and offboarding.

 - Coordinate new hire onboarding to ensure employees have a smooth and engaging start at Harper.

 - Maintain accurate employee records, HR systems, personnel files, and employment documentation.

 - Prepare offer letters, employment letters, and other HR-related documentation.

 - Manage day-to-day HR operations and respond to employee queries related to policies, benefits, leave, and HR processes.

 - Coordinate with payroll and benefits providers to ensure accurate and timely administration.

 - Support leave management, employee data updates, and other HR administrative processes.

3. Employee Experience & Engagement

 - Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees on day-to-day HR matters.

 - Support employee engagement initiatives, team activities, and culture-building programs.

 - Help organize employee surveys and identify opportunities to improve the employee experience.

 - Support performance review cycles, feedback processes, and employee development initiatives.

 - Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and people-first work environment.

4. HR Policies & Compliance

 - Support the implementation and communication of HR policies, procedures, and employee guidelines.

 - Maintain and update HR documentation and the employee handbook.

 - Help ensure compliance with applicable employment laws and internal policies.

 - Handle sensitive employee information with confidentiality and discretion.

 - Identify opportunities to simplify and improve HR workflows and processes.

5. People Programs & Process Improvement

 - Partner with the VP of People on initiatives across talent acquisition, employee experience, and People Operations.

 - Build and maintain recruiting and HR dashboards to track key metrics.

 - Identify opportunities to streamline processes and improve operational efficiency.

 - Support the development of scalable People practices as Harper grows.

Qualifications & Experience

 - 3 years of experience in HR Generalist, Talent Acquisition, or People Operations roles.

 - Experience managing end-to-end recruitment for technical and non-technical roles, preferably in a technology or SaaS company.

 - Solid understanding of core HR processes and the employee lifecycle.

 - Strong sourcing, candidate assessment, stakeholder management, and communication skills.

 - Ability to manage multiple open roles and HR priorities simultaneously.

 - Comfortable working with hiring managers, employees, and senior leadership.

 - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and a high sense of ownership.

 - A hands-on, resourceful mindset and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

 - High integrity and discretion when handling confidential information.

What Success Looks Like

 - Hiring managers receive proactive recruiting support and positions move efficiently through the hiring process.

 - Candidates have a positive and consistent recruitment experience.

 - New hires experience seamless onboarding and are set up for success.

 - Employees receive timely and effective support on HR-related matters.

 - HR operations and employee records remain accurate, organized, and compliant.

 - Recruiting and HR processes become increasingly efficient and scalable as Harper grows.

Why Join Harper?

 - Play a dual-impact role across talent acquisition and HR.

 - Work closely with the VP of People, hiring managers, and leadership.

 - Take ownership of meaningful initiatives in a growing company.

 - Help shape both the talent Harper attracts and the employee experience it creates.
